messages:
maya: quick q — ran a restore drill for tenant-42 blobstore snapshot and hit a KMS decrypt AccessDenied on the restore-runner SA. snapshot metadata shows cmk: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01. who owns the backup uploader grant lifecycle? cc @kevin @sam :thinking:
enc-bot: [alert] kms:Decrypt failed for requestId=fd3a... user=restore-runner principal=arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/restore-runner action=Decrypt :rotating_light:
kevin: can you paste the exact error lines? also which account did the snapshot originate from — same account or cross-account?
sam: backup-agent uploads snapshots in customer-account A and creates a one-off grant for restore-runner (infra account) with expiry. we also run a weekly grant-prune job that removes expired grants. if the CMK was rotated and we rekeyed files, old grants might've been pruned incorrectly.
maya: here's the log snippet:
```
"KMSAccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/restore-runner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"
```
kevin: ok. two quick checks: 1) cloudtrail for kms:CreateGrant/CreateRetireGrant around snapshot time, 2) check key policy if it allows createGrant from backup-agent principal. also confirm if grant-prune job ran after rotation.
jordan: also check s3 object metadata for x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id and x-amz-server-side-encryption; if object was re-uploaded with new key id we may need a rewrap step. we should capture cloudtrail eventIds for audit.
sam: note: only key owner (account 123456789012 or principals allowed by key policy) can create grants. if snapshot lived in customer-account but restore-runner is in infra account we rely on a cross-account grant or CMK key policy to allow CreateGrant by backup-agent. if rotation changed key alias/ARN, prune job may have removed old grants believing they were stale.
maya: so immediate ask: can we provision a temp grant so restore completes? and longer term: change RBAC so backup-uploader always creates a durable cross-account grant that survives rotation?
kevin: short-term fix: owner of CMK (acct 123456789012) can run:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-ef01 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/restore-runner --operations Decrypt --name "temp-restore-grant"
```
that will let the restore-runner decrypt. but remember to retire-grant after. i'll do this if we confirm owner contact. :+1:
sam: long-term options: 1) use envelope keys where upload is encrypted under a per-tenant data key that we control and rewrap into CMK so rekeying doesn't invalidate grants; 2) give backup-agent permission to recreate grants post-rotation and mark grants with metadata so prune job doesn't remove them; 3) change prune job to consult rotation logs instead of TTL only.
jordan: also add CloudTrail alerts for CreateGrant/RetireGrant anomalies and add a test to our restore acceptance: rotate CMK then run restore. feature flag in CI.
maya: sounds good. can someone own the post-mortem & playbook updates? i'll record this as a drill and link to runbook.
kevin: i'll take the short-term grant creation now and update the playbook with the create-grant step + required audit checks. will also file a ticket to change prune logic.
sam: i'll work on redesigning the grant lifecycle so backup-agent can safely recreate grants and mark them as persistent during rotation flows.
jordan: i'll add alerting for unexpected kms:Decrypt failures targeting snapshot restores and a CI test.
maya: thanks all. tagging incident-sim channel to schedule a formal drill next week. :calendar:
kevin: quick note — remember cross-account restore may also require key policy updates: if restore-runner role isn't listed, create-grant won't help. i'll verify key policy before creating grant.
maya: copied. i'll post the timeline and the cloudtrail event ids when i have them. thanks! :heart:
